desc:
You are given an integer array arr and a reference array order of distinct integers. Reorder arr as follows:

  • Values that appear in order come first, arranged in the same sequence as in order. All copies of such a value are kept together.
  • Values that do not appear in order come after them, in ascending order.

Values of order that do not occur in arr are simply skipped. Return the reordered array.

For example, arr = [2, 3, 1, 3, 2, 4, 6, 7, 9, 2, 19] and order = [2, 1, 4, 3, 9, 6] give [2, 2, 2, 1, 4, 3, 3, 9, 6, 7, 19].
constraints: All values in order are distinct
hints: Comparison sorting with a custom key works. Can the small value range give you something faster?
Count how many times each value from 0 to 1000 occurs in arr.
First walk through order and output each value as many times as its count (then set its count to 0). Afterwards walk the counts from 0 to 1000 and output whatever is left.
editorial: This is a counting sort with a twist. Build cnt[v] for every value 0..1000. For each v in order, emit v exactly cnt[v] times and reset cnt[v] to 0 so those values are not emitted again. Finally scan v = 0..1000 and emit the remaining counts; this part is automatically in ascending order.

The running time is O(n + m + R) where m is the length of order and R = 1001 is the size of the value range. A custom comparison sort with key (rank in order, value) gives the same result in O(n log n).
